personaSeed: You are a careful academic researcher. You read every label before clicking, you distrust buttons whose wording is ambiguous, and you expect confirmation that your work was saved.

findings.summary: The brief explicitly asked to weigh in on the look before anything gets built, yet on first visit the pipeline already showed Build with 3 tasks running before the user had seen or reacted to any mockup.

After the user requested a design change, the newly generated version (v3) appeared already marked 'approved' with the Approve button disabled — the user never approved the revised design and was given no way to; the approval act happens without them.

The 'Open in focus mode' buttons on design cards are hover-revealed and sit behind the Critique panel at default viewport size, so clicking them times out; three attempts failed until the viewport was enlarged and the card body was clicked instead.

After the requested change finished generating (v3 present, status back to 'approved'), the prompt bar still showed a 'Stop' button instead of 'Send', leaving it ambiguous whether generation was still running.

The Promote to build confirmation explains itself in internal jargon — 'compiles and signs the contract, freezes the oracle' — which a first-time user cannot interpret before a consequential, hard-to-reverse action.

The core flow succeeded end to end: prototypes were on screen, one pointed reaction produced a new version (v3, '1 file(s) from prompt'), the design baseline was frozen as approved, and Confirm and compile landed the build tasks on the Board.
